critique:
field buttons_pressed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: in every episode the goal asks for both buttons first, then container pick-ups. The step after A shows the gripper descending onto the first button (either a frame saying the button 'is pressed down', or the gripper within a few pixels of the button's [y, x] at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed); the step after B shows the same on the other button. The recorded subgoal at the step showing the second press is already C at the first named color's container. But the annotated count was filled one step late: 0 at the step that shows the first press, 1 at the step that shows the second press, 2 only at the step after that. So the policy, following its instruction, wrote 1 at the step showing the first press and the record said 0 (PREDICTABILITY), and at the step showing the second press the annotated 1 could not justify C under the subgoal rules that need 2 (SUFFICIENCY). The phrase 'at the step after the first such frame' was read as 'the step after the step containing that frame'. Change: buttons_pressed holds the number of button presses whose execution frames have been shown at or before this step. It changes value at the step whose own execution frames show a press, not at the next step. 0 at the first step (no execution frames); 1 at the step whose frames show the first press (normally the step right after A); 2 at the step whose frames show the second press (normally the step right after B), and 2 at every later step. A press is a frame saying a button 'is pressed down', or the gripper within about 6 px of a button's [y, x] at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed; the gripper lowering onto a container (height around 0.1, 20 px or more from any button, button merely missing from the list because it is occluded) is not a press. Safety net: at any step whose frames show a container 'held in the gripper' or the gripper lowered onto a container, the value is 2 whatever the earlier count. e.g. 2

field red_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: after the red container had been lifted and the red cube seen beneath it, the next step showed the held container being lowered back onto the cube, with the cube visible in an early frame and only containers in the last frames; the policy chained containers and wrote the set-down container's position, or at the lifting step wrote the held container's own position, instead of the cube's last visible position. The record kept the cube position. PREDICTABILITY. Change: no new content, but precedence must be stated first for every color field: if the color is already in picked_colors, or any frame of this step shows that cube itself (container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), the field is the cube's position in the last frame where the cube is visible and the container chain is not run for that color at this step or any later step; the held container's position and the position of a container set back down on the cube are never written. e.g. [101, 165]

field buttons_pressed, POLICY PROMPT
  The policy's count was right and the record was late; now the record counts at the step whose frames show the press, so the instruction stays as a per-step increment but must be stated plainly with the press test and the exclusion: write 0 at the first step (empty memory, no execution frames). Otherwise write the carried count plus 1 if any execution frame of this step says a button 'is pressed down' OR shows the gripper within about 6 px of a button's [y, x] at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed; a frame with the gripper over a container (height around 0.1, 20 px or more from the nearest button) is not a press even if a button is missing from the list in that frame. Each step shows at most one press, so the count never rises by more than 1. If any frame of this step shows a container 'held in the gripper' or the gripper lowered onto a container with fingers closing, write 2 regardless of the carried count, because both presses precede any pick-up. e.g. 2

field green_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Put the cube rule first, before the chain procedure, for all three color fields: if green is already in the carried picked_colors, or any frame of this step shows the green cube itself (its container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), do not chain containers for green; write the cube's position from the last frame in which the cube is visible, and keep that position at every later step even when a container is set down over it and only containers are listed in the last frames. Never write the position of a container 'held in the gripper'. Only then, for colors not yet exposed, run the chain exactly as described. e.g. [105, 161]

field red_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Same reordering as green_container: the exposed-cube rule comes first and freezes the field. If red is in the carried picked_colors or the red cube is visible in any frame of this step, write the cube's last visible position and ignore every container, including the held one and the one lowered back onto the cube; otherwise chain as before. e.g. [101, 165]

field blue_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Same reordering as green_container: the exposed-cube rule comes first and freezes the field. If blue is in the carried picked_colors or the blue cube is visible in any frame of this step, write the cube's last visible position and ignore every container, including the held one and the one lowered back onto the cube; otherwise chain as before. e.g. [102, 79]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The ordering of rules sent the policy wrong twice over. First, rule 2 (buttons_pressed is 1 → B) stood before rule 3 (container held → D), so at the step where the container had just been lifted with the cube visible beneath it, a count of 1 produced B instead of D. The held-container rule must be the first rule after the first-step rule: if the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper', answer D whatever buttons_pressed reads. Second, with the count now written at the step whose frames show the press, the button rules read: if buttons_pressed after this step's update is 1, answer B; if it is 2 and nothing is held, go to the pick-up rules (C at the first named color's container when picked_colors is empty, C at the second named color's container when picked_colors has one entry and the goal names a second cube, D when every named cube is picked). Remove the sentence saying that at any step with execution frames a count of 0 or 1 means B; a count of 0 at a step with execution frames can no longer occur, and 1 means exactly one press shown so far. The point for C stays the color's container value written at this step. The fallback stays as it is.

refused
  Several steps asked for new machinery to repair a 'stale' carried count: a list of pressed button positions, a rule that any step with execution frames implies A's press even if unseen, and a rule that a press on a button different from the first one means both are done. All of these were reactions to the one-step lag in how the count was annotated; once the count is written at the step whose frames show the press, the carried value is 1 after the first press and 2 after the second, and the plain count settles every step in the minibatch. A list of button positions would duplicate the count and is not needed. One step claimed a press should be detected when a button disappears from the list while the gripper is lowered about 20 px away at height around 0.1 with fingers closed; in that episode the gripper was closing on a container next to the button, which was merely occluded, and the real second press had been shown in the previous step. That heuristic would count false presses and is not passed on; the opposite exclusion is added instead. Suggestions that buttons_pressed should be incremented one step later or only at the second press are dropped: the record, not the policy, was late, and the rule is changed to match the policy's reading.

critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: It told me to add 1 when any execution frame shows the gripper at a button's [y, x] at height below 0.06 with fingers closed; t=80 shows exactly that (gripper [62, 148], height 0.027, fingers 0% open, button at [65, 147]), so I wrote 1, yet the recorded value is 0. The instruction needs to say what actually counts as a press for buttons_pressed at this step: either that the gripper-lowered-on-button frames do NOT count and only an explicit 'is pressed down' label (or a button changing state) increments the field, or that the increment is deferred to the next decision step; as written it contradicts the recorded value.

critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: It did not say how to recover a wrong carried count: when the frames of a step show a press on one button while the gripper enters the step hovering over or retreating from the OTHER button (first frame at height ~0.15 within a few px in x of it), both buttons have been pressed and buttons_pressed must be written 2 regardless of the carried value; and the first step must write 1 if its frames already show the first press.
critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_subgoal: It did not say that a step whose frames show a button press while the gripper started the step at the other button is the completion of the second press, so the next subgoal is C at the remembered container of the first color named in the goal (red_container), even if buttons_pressed after the update reads only 1; rule 2 sent me to B on a count that was stale.

critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: The press-detection criterion did not fit this step: the press at t=304 shows the gripper at [87, 168], height 0.106, fingers 0% open, roughly 20 px from the button at [63, 147], and the button itself VANISHES from the button list at that frame (and again at t=352 while the gripper stays low beside it). The instruction should say that a button dropping out of the listed buttons while the gripper is lowered near it (within ~25 px, height below ~0.12) with fingers closing counts as a press, and that a step can contain both a press and a later pick-up, so count the press even when the step ends with a container held.

It should state that a container 'held in the gripper' at the final scene always takes precedence and means D, regardless of the button count, and that execution frames showing the gripper descending onto a container with a cube exposed beneath it prove the button phase is finished (set buttons_pressed=2 if still 1 before applying the rules).

critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: It told me to write carried-in count plus 1 because t=80 shows 'button at [63, 153] is pressed down' (and the gripper at the button at height 0.024 with fingers closed), so I wrote buttons_pressed=1, but the recorded value is 0. Either the annotator prompt counts a press at a different moment (e.g. only after the button stays shown as pressed at the decision-step scene, or only when the second button is pressed, or the count is incremented one step later) or the recorded 0 is wrong; the instruction and the rule disagree on when the first press is counted, and the instruction must state the same moment as the rule.
